key_insight: Density-dependent, strain-limiting elasticity bounds local deformation near static crack tips while sustaining equilibrium through intense localized stresses.
engineering_relevance: The model supports analysis of how crack geometry and applied load distribution jointly shape near-tip stress, strain, and energy localization.
method: Formulate nonlinear hyperelasticity with material moduli coupled to volumetric strain.
Establish weak-solution existence and uniqueness using the Minty–Browder theorem.
Solve with damped Newton–Raphson linearization and conforming hp-adaptive finite elements.
evidence_signal: Numerical comparisons span five boundary-loading profiles and variations in the density-dependent parameter, tracking near-tip normal stress, normal strain, and strain energy density.
watch_item: The abstract reports stationary-crack simulations, not experimental validation or crack-growth predictions.
paper_title: hp-Adaptive Finite Element Modeling of Static Cracks in Density-Dependent Media
